items.author: shadeaurion.bsky.social
items.context: Oh dude, don't stress. Its why GoG is good. To be fair, Itch deserves a mention. I've seen games start and grow there and become huge indie hits everywhere else. Faith, Mindustry, that one sick game where you're a skateboarding racoon doing tricks through dimensions to save the world. Tanuki Sunset?
items.text: Fair point on Itch. A lot of games there are DRM-free too, so you can download the files and keep them.

items.author: freshroyal.bsky.social
items.context: I've wanted to play it since release, but I just never got around to getting a copy. Thinking about buying it during the Steam Winter Sale this year. It's also *kind of* a multi-platform Nintendo game, and that's funny.
items.text: Winter Sale is a solid plan. Add it to your wishlist now and Steam will notify you when it goes on sale.

items.author: ajisaivt.vtubers.social
items.context: Might I suggest Critically Acclaimed MM-! JK, Honestly, when I need time off to settle my head, I lean towards lookin' at my backlog, be it games I wanted to play on my own time, or manga recommendations I've been sittin' on. Or just re-watching old web shows or abridged series to brain off.
items.text: Backlog dives are great for that. Pick something short and low-pressure when your head needs a reset.

items.author: maddyjacksonn.bsky.social
items.context: i wasn't going to buy it at launch and instead wait for a sale bc i'm skeptical of the setting and it being "my kinda game", but after watching a bit, the amount of player freedom [similar to RDR2] seems like my kinda thing???? i didn't really get that outta my playthrough of GTAV
items.text: Smart to wait if you're not sure it's your kind of game. Checking the price history before a sale shows you what a real low looks like.
